diagnostic_evidence.quote: For $\gamma_\star>0$ it is straightforward to see that $\gbd$ satisfies  Assumption~\ref{assump:gbd-mon} with $r = 2$.
regularising this as above yields that $\Seps$ satisfies Assumption~\ref{assump:gbd-reg} (see Example \ref{ex:reg-rel}).

issues.failure_explanation: Assumption (A2) (and its regularised counterpart (a2)) requires $\bs\cdot\bv \ge c(|\bs|^{r'}+|\bv|^r-1)$ at every graph point. Both the stick-slip graph \eqref{def:Tresca} and the shifted graph of \eqref{eq:nonmon-impl} contain points with $\bu_\tau = 0$ and $|\bs|$ up to $\mu_\star$ resp. $\mu(0)=a$; there $\bs\cdot\bv = 0$, so the inequality can hold only if $\mu_\star \le 1$ resp. $a \le 1$. For larger intercepts these relations satisfy (A2)/(a2) for no exponent $r$ (stick-slip also fails the $r=1$ branch because $|\bs|$ is unbounded), unless the parameters degenerate to the pure Tresca law. Hence the coverage claims in Examples `ex:Tresca` (stick-slip with $r=2$) and `ex:Fang` are false as stated, and the numerical section's assertion that the regularised Fang relation (with $a=1.6>1$) satisfies Assumption `assump:gbd-reg` is likewise false.

failure_location.quote: Hence, the implicit relation can be cast in the form~\eqref{itm:case-impl-coerc-1} with $\gbd$ satisfying Assumption~\ref{assump:gbd-mon} with $r = 2$ and $\lambda$ as above.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the '$-1$' normalization in (A2) and (a2) by an independent additive constant, i.e. $\bs\cdot\bv \ge c_1|\bs|^{r'} + c_1|\bv|^r - c_2$ (with the analogous $r=1$ variant); all subsequent arguments (a priori estimates, Browder-type citations, Yosida approximation) use only this two-constant form, so every proof, theorem and example, including stick-slip with arbitrary $\mu_\star$ and the Fang relation with arbitrary $a$, is preserved.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised coverage of stick-slip boundary conditions with $\mu_\star>1$ and of non-monotone implicit (Fang-type) relations with $\mu(0)>1$ by the convergence theory (Theorems `thm:main-unsteady`, `thm:main-unsteady-v` via case (C2)) is unsupported as written, and the numerical experiment of Section 6.1.2 is performed with parameters outside the stated assumptions.
issues.title: Coercivity assumption (A2)/(a2) with '-1' normalization is violated by the claimed stick-slip and Fang-type relations
issues.why_classification: The defect is a constant-normalization in the assumption's statement; the two-constant repair is short and local, requires no new argument anywhere, and restores every advertised coverage claim and guarantee.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: $\mathcal{R}(\Omega) \coloneqq \operatorname{ker} \BD = \{\bx \mapsto A\bx + \bb \text{ for some } A \in \setR^{d \times d} \text{ with } A = -A^\top \text{ and } \bb \in \setR^d \}$
For the supplementary statement, we use the preceding inequality on each of the finitely many connected components and sum over the latter.

issues.failure_explanation: For disconnected $\Omega$ the distributional kernel of $\BD$ consists of piecewise rigid motions (one affine map per component), which strictly contains the globally affine maps in the displayed definition of $\mathcal{R}(\Omega)$; the two coincide only for connected $\Omega$. Reading $\mathcal{R}(\Omega)$ as the globally affine maps, the supplementary claim is false: for $\Omega$ the union of three disjoint balls in $\mathbb{R}^3$ with non-collinear centres, Assumption `assump:dom` holds (a global $Ax+b$ with zero normal trace on all three spheres satisfies $Ax_i+b=0$, $i=1,2,3$, whence $A=0$, $b=0$), yet the function $u$ equal to a rotation about the first ball's centre on that component and zero elsewhere lies in $W^{1,p}(\Omega)^d$ with $\BD u = 0$ and $\tr(u)\cdot\bn = 0$ on $\Gamma$ but $u \ne 0$, contradicting \eqref{eq:kornetto0}. The component-wise argument in the proof needs the normal trace to be a norm on each component's rigid motions, an omitted hypothesis not implied by the stated assumption.

failure_location.quote: The same conclusion holds true if $\Omega\subset\R^{d}$ is open and bounded with Lipschitz boundary and has finitely many connected components.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define $\mathcal{R}(\Omega)$ as the full (piecewise) kernel of $\BD$ when $\Omega$ is disconnected — equivalently, require in Assumption `assump:dom` that the normal trace be a norm on the piecewise rigid motions — so that extending a component-wise rigid motion by zero makes the sketched component-wise proof valid.
issues.overall_effect: Only the supplementary side statement about domains with finitely many connected components is affected; all applications in the paper use connected domains, so no downstream result is impacted.
issues.title: Supplementary multi-component statement of the Korn theorem is false under the displayed definition of rigid deformations
issues.why_classification: The false statement is an unused supplementary remark; the repair is a local definitional change with no effect on any other result, application, or guarantee.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \bv \mapsto \norm{\bv \cdot \bn}_{L^q(\Gamma)}\qquad \text{is a norm on the  rigid deformations $\mathcal{R}(\Omega)$}
Thanks to Corollary~\ref{cor:polyhedral}, Assumption~\ref{assump:dom} holds for~$\Gamma = \partial \Omega$ for a polyhedral domain~$\Omega$ as in Theorem~\ref{thm:main-unsteady}.
If $\Gamma\subset\partial\Omega$ is polyhedral and contains two non-collinear normals $\bn(x),\bn(\widetilde{x})$ as indicated for $x$ and $\widetilde{x}$, Assumption \ref{assump:dom} is satisfied.

issues.failure_explanation:
Assumption `assump:dom` concerns only the normal component of the trace, but the proof assumes the rigid motion $\pi$ vanishes identically on $\Gamma$ — a much stronger hypothesis — so it establishes a different (trivial) statement. Moreover, the corollary itself is false for $d\ge 3$: on a flat piece with normal $
u$, $ rho\cdot
u=0$ for $ rho(x)=Ax+b$ only forces $A
u=0$ and $b\cdot
u=0$; with only two non-collinear normals, any translation $b$ orthogonal to both (which exists whenever $d\ge 3$) is a nonzero rigid motion with zero normal trace on $\Gamma_1\cup\Gamma_2$. Concrete counterexample: $\Omega$ the unit cube in $\mathbb{R}^3$, $\Gamma_1$ the face $\{z=0\}$, $\Gamma_2$ the face $\{y=0\}$, and $ rho \equiv e_1$. The claim is true only for $d=2$.

failure_location.quote: Let $A\in\R^{d\times d}$ be skew-symmetric,  $b\in\R^d$, and suppose that $\pi(x)\coloneqq Ax+b$ satisfies $\pi=0$ on $\Gamma$, whereby $\pi=0$ on $H_{1}\cup H_{2}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair:
Restate the corollary with a hypothesis that actually suffices — e.g. that the normals of the flat pieces of $\Gamma$ span $\mathbb{R}^d$ (in particular $\Gamma=\partial\Omega$ of a bounded polyhedron, as used throughout in $d\in\{2,3\}$) — and replace the proof by the normal-component argument ($ rho\cdot
u=0$ on a flat piece forces $A
u=0$ and $b\cdot
u=0$); all applications are then covered unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The corollary, the accompanying figure caption, Remark `rmk:mixed-bc`'s justification of Assumption `assump:dom` for $\Gamma=\partial\Omega$, and the polyhedral normal-trace assertion on which the proof of `lem:h-norm` relies become unreliable; hence the availability of the Korn inequality underpinning the a priori estimates and both main convergence theorems lacks its stated justification (the needed fact for $\Gamma=\partial\Omega$ of a bounded polyhedron is nevertheless true, since the facet normals positively span $\mathbb{R}^d$).
issues.title: Polyhedral-domain corollary (two non-collinear normals) is false for $d\ge 3$ and its proof assumes vanishing of the full trace
issues.why_classification: The stated corollary is false in the paper's main dimension $d=3$ and its proof argues from a different hypothesis, so both statement and proof must be reworked and the hypothesis weakened (two non-collinear normals to spanning normals); the repair is, however, contained, and since the full-boundary case used throughout is genuinely true, no main theorem loses scope or needs new proof architecture.

issues.failure_explanation: With $\xi^k(t)=\int_0^t\pi^k$, Hardy's inequality gives $\|\xi^k\|_{L^{8/(d+4)}(I;L^2)}^{8/(d+4)} \le C_T\|\pi^k\|_{L^{8/(d+4)}(I;L^2)}^{8/(d+4)} = C_T\,\delta_k\sum_j\|\pi^k_j\|^{8/(d+4)}$, whereas Lemma `lem:p-est` controls only $\delta_k^2\sum_j\|\pi^k_j\|^{8/(d+4)}$, i.e. $\|\pi^k\|_{L^{8/(d+4)}(I;L^2)} \le (c/\delta_k)^{(d+4)/8}$, which diverges. Indeed, the $\delta^2$-weighted bound is compatible with data for which $\|\xi^k(T)\|_{L^2(\Omega)}$ diverges, so the claimed uniform bound on $\xi^k$ is not implied by the cited lemma. The bound (in fact $\sup_t\|\xi^k(t)\|_{L^2(\Omega)}\le c$) is true, but requires a different argument: summing the discrete equations over the time steps before applying the discrete inf-sup, which eliminates the $\delta_k^{-1}\|u^k_j-u^k_{j-1}\|_B$ term that forced the $\delta^2$-weighting.

failure_location.quote: By Lemma~\ref{lem:p-est} we have that \begin{align}\label{eq:est-press-4} \norm{\xi^k}_{L^{8/(d+4)}(I;L^2(\Omega))} \leq c, \end{align} uniformly in $k$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Insert the missing argument: multiply the discrete scheme by $\delta_k$ and sum over $j \le J$, test with $v_h \in X_h \cap H^1_0(\Omega)^d$, and apply the discrete inf-sup of Assumption `assump:fem`(iii) to $\xi^k(t_J) = \delta_k\sum_{j\le J}\pi^k_j$, bounding every term by $c\|v_h\|_{X_h}$ via the a priori estimates; this yields $\sup_t\|\xi^k(t)\|_{L^2(\Omega)} \le c$, after which the lemma and all downstream results proceed unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The weak convergence $\xi^k \rightharpoonup \xi$ and hence the passage to the limit in the pressure term of the discrete equation (step \eqref{eq:unst-lim-4} of Proposition `prop:limit-eq`), the derivation of the limiting equation and energy identity, and thereby both main convergence theorems, rest on an unjustified step.
issues.title: Uniform bound on the pressure primitive in the pressure-convergence lemma does not follow from the cited pressure estimate
issues.why_classification: A necessary step of the proof is invalid as written and must be replaced by a different, contained but nontrivial argument; the lemma's statement and all dependent results remain true and unchanged, so the repair involves a local replacement argument rather than any mathematical loss or new global architecture.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The slip boundary is taken to be the top wall~$\Gamma_s = (0,1)\times \{1\}$ and no-slip conditions are imposed on the complement~$\Gamma_d\coloneqq \partial\Omega \setminus \Gamma_s$.
We choose~$a=1.0$, $b=0.1$, $c=0.001$, $\theta=-0.75$; with this choice the relation is indeed non-monotone.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose asserts that the Taylor–Green pair $(\hat{\bu},\hat{p})$ is a manufactured (exact) solution of the computed boundary value problem. It is not: on $\Gamma_s$ ($y=1$) one has $\hat{\bu}_\tau = -\Lambda_\star\sin(\pi x)e_1 \ne 0$ while $-(2\BD\hat{\bu}\,\bn)_\tau \equiv 0$ there ($\BD\hat{\bu}$ is diagonal on $y=1$ and $2\BD\hat{\bu}\,e_2$ is parallel to $\bn$), so the constitutive relation \eqref{eq:non-monotone-slip} with $a,c>0$ is violated; on $\Gamma_d$ (the walls $x\in\{0,1\}$ and $y=0$) $\hat{\bu}$ does not vanish, violating the imposed no-slip condition. Hence no exact solution of the computed problem is known and the forcing merely drives the flow (in contrast to Section 6.1.2, where $\hat{\bu}|_{\partial\Omega}=\bm{0}$ makes the manufactured-solution argument valid for small $\Lambda_\star$).

failure_location.quote: The forcing term in the momentum equation is determined by $\bm{f} \coloneqq - 2\diver( \BD\hat{\bu}) + \diver(\hat{\bu}\otimes \hat{\bu}) + \nabla \hat{p}$, i.e., we work with  a manufactured solution.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Delete or correct the phrase 'i.e., we work with a manufactured solution', stating instead that the forcing is derived from a Taylor–Green vortex in order to drive a flow with nontrivial tangential velocity on $\Gamma_s$, while the exact solution of the slip problem is unknown.
issues.overall_effect: The reader is misled about what the experiment of Section 6.1.1 computes and validates (no reference solution exists for it); the qualitative conclusions drawn from the constitutive-relation plots are unaffected.
issues.title: Claim that the smooth non-monotone slip experiment uses a manufactured solution is false
issues.why_classification: A single mischaracterizing sentence; removing or correcting it preserves every computation, figure, and conclusion of the numerical section.
